title: Optimizer hints (MySQL) vs the PostgreSQL planner
claim: Force index usage or join order when the optimizer makes a bad choice; use sparingly.
verdict: PostgreSQL has no hints, and here it did not need them. The planner's choice ({t:planner_choice}) beat the
alternatives it had rejected: bitmap scan + sort {t:no_index_scan}, full scan {t:seqscan_only}. The enable_*
switches are an experiment tool to see those alternatives, not a production fix; when the planner picks badly,
fix statistics (demo 01) or indexes first. The pg_hint_plan extension exists if hints are really needed.
